sentences.text: The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973("Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 62/2014 registered at Police Station Chhawala, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all other proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Manoj Pant, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Rakesh Kumar Lakra and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Dharamveer from Police Station Chhawala, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that respondent no.2 got married with the son of petitioner no.1.
One child master Yug was born out of the said wedlock.

It is stated that husband of the respondent no.2 was addicted of alcohol and due to his addiction disputes arose amongst the petitioners and respondent no.2 whereupon respondent no. 2 lodged a complaint against the petitioners and her husband and the present FIR bearing no. 62/2014 registered at Police Station Chhawala, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC was registered.
It is stated that during the investigation, husband of the respondent no.2 had died.

Thereafter, with the intervention of well wishers and common friends, parties arrived at amicable settlement vide Settlement Agreement dated 17.02.2018 before the Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. It is stated that the husband of complainant had passed away prior to the settlement arrived at in the present case.
It is stated that the share in the property of the husband of complainant has already been transferred to the minor son.
The complainant is present, who states that nothing remains to be received in the present case and she has no objection, if the FIR is quashed.

sentences.text: In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

7. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 62/2014 registered at Police Station Chhawala, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
8. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
9. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 19, 2023/
